question: Does any candidate language match Linear A better than a permuted control?

protocol.null: frequency_matched is the headline; breadth_matched retained for comparison
protocol.calibration: Greek is a known-false control. Its score under the strongest null is the artifact benchmark any hypothesis must beat.
protocol.hit: any candidate skeleton attested in that hypothesis's lexicon
protocol.note: Each hypothesis is scored against its own null; raw rates are not comparable across lexicons.

blocked.label: Anatolian (Luwian / Lycian)
blocked.blocker: No openly licensed machine-readable Luwian or Hittite lexicon located. The Chicago Hittite Dictionary is not open. Candidate: eDiAna (Munich) — check terms.

blocked.label: Tyrsenian (Etruscan / Lemnian)
blocked.blocker: Etruscan corpus is small and glosses are contested. Candidate: the Etruscan Texts Project or CIE digitisations — licensing unverified.

blocked.label: Uralic / "West-Ugric"
blocked.blocker: Revesz builds his own dictionary, which is the core objection to the work. A fair test needs an independent Uralic root list (Finnish/Hungarian/Proto-Uralic) not assembled to fit. Candidate: Uralonet (Budapest) — terms unverified.

mainstream.label: Mainstream Aegean scholarship
mainstream.source: Duhoux 2004, Younger, Monti 2022, Salgarella 2025, Davis 2026 — the consensus that Minoan is unidentified, probably non-Indo-European and non-Semitic, possibly an isolate, with no theory holding an edge.

uniform.label: Uniform — no prior commitment
uniform.source: Deliberately uninformative. The default when reporting to a general audience.

semitic_advocate.label: Maximally favourable to the Semitic hypothesis
semitic_advocate.source: The weighting a proponent of di Mino 2026 or Gordon 1966 might hold. Included so the Semitic result can be reported under priors its own advocates would accept — if the evidence fails to move the posterior even here, the finding is robust.

indo_european_advocate.label: Maximally favourable to an Indo-European reading
indo_european_advocate.source: Palmer 1958, Owens 1996, Finkelberg 2001 — the Anatolian and Greek-related lines.

sceptical.label: Corpus-too-small scepticism
sceptical.source: Shannon's unicity distance applied to ~7,500 signs with no parallel text, plus Braović 2024 challenge #4 ("might be impossible") and Barber's provability threshold. The position that no hypothesis is currently distinguishable.
